title: An open immersion is fully faithful on the derived categories
statement:
For an open immersion $g:V\hookrightarrow T$, the derived functors satisfy

$$
Lg^*Rg_*\cong\operatorname{id},
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
Lg^*i_*=0
$$

for the closed complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ of $g$.

proof.text: At the abelian-sheaf level, [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] gives the adjunction $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$, while [lem-sc-open-immersion-pushforward-fully-faithful] says that for an open immersion the counit $g^{-1}g_*G	o G$ is an isomorphism for every sheaf $G$ on $V$. The inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact], so [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] identifies its termwise functor on complexes with the derived functor $Lg^*$.

source.place: proof paragraph: the sheaf-level inverse/direct-image adjunction and open-immersion counit

proof.text: For a complex $K$ on $V$, choose a quasi-isomorphism $K	o I$ with $I$ K-injective using [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The total right derived functor of the direct-image functor exists and is computed on such an $I$ by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], so $Rg_*K$ is represented by the complex $g_*I$. Moreover [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] applies because $g_*$ is right adjoint to the exact functor $g^{-1}$, and therefore $g_*I$ is K-injective; [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] supplies the derived-category Hom identification and hence the naturality in $K$.

source.place: proof paragraph: K-injective resolutions and derived direct image

proof.text: Applying the termwise representative from the preceding steps gives $Lg^*Rg_*K\simeq Q(g^{-1}g_*I)$. The counit isomorphism of [lem-sc-open-immersion-pushforward-fully-faithful] is natural in $I$, hence gives an isomorphism of complexes $g^{-1}g_*I\cong I$; applying the derived localization yields $Lg^*Rg_*K\cong K$. The resolution-independence and functoriality are those in [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], so these isomorphisms assemble to the asserted natural isomorphism $Lg^*Rg_*\cong\operatorname{id}$.

For the scheme-theoretic closed complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$, the disjointness of the ranges and the open-immersion hypothesis give $g^{-1}i_*\mathcal H=0$ for every sheaf $\mathcal H$ by [lemma-openclosed-vanishing-lowerstar]. Here $i_*$ on complexes is the termwise closed-immersion direct image (the $i_*$ occurring in the displayed identity), so applying the sheaf-level identity in every degree gives the zero complex. Since $g^{-1}$ is exact and its derived functor is represented termwise by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], this zero complex represents $Lg^*i_*$. Thus the second displayed identity $Lg^*i_*=0$ follows.
